evidence: The survivor initializes "single terminal masks" and uses "full = (1 << t) - 1" with subset DP, which is the standard exact Steiner-tree algorithm.
affordance_in_statement: Each available option allows you to add a specific vector of the form b_u + b_v ... since the field is GF(2), addition is commutative ... You must ensure that for every pair of priority coordinates x and y, the vector b_x + b_y is contained in V.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: over GF(2), the span of vectors b_u+b_v is intrinsically the even-parity subspace of each connected component, so requiring all priority pairs forces those vertices into one connected component. Removing this reduction would require changing the vector construction or the required subspace.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the minimum selected edge set is a minimum-weight Steiner tree connecting all priority vertices and solves it with subset DP over terminal masks.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The available vectors are exactly pair-incidence vectors b_u+b_v over GF(2), and every pair of priority coordinates must lie in the generated row space.

common_affordance: The GF(2) span of pair vectors b_u+b_v is characterized by graph connectivity, reducing the problem to a minimum-weight Steiner tree connecting all priority coordinates.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It computes shortest-path distances between priority vertices and then treats those distances as sufficient, which ignores the possibility of sharing nonterminal Steiner vertices and edges across several connections.
It uses a union-find/MST-style approach on the priority coordinates, effectively requiring direct terminal connectivity and missing cheaper Steiner trees through nonpriority coordinates.
Its comments and implementation build an MST on the priority vertices rather than solving the general Steiner-tree problem over all n vertices.

recommended_edit: No safe edit can defeat the surviving solver while preserving the mathematical task. Any effective edit would have to change the core pair-vector construction or the row-space requirement, such as replacing b_u+b_v by a different class of vectors; that would make it a different problem.
regression_risk: Any edit that removes the connectivity characterization changes the problem rather than merely closing a shortcut, and could invalidate the examples and no longer measure the intended task.
